page_title: Qbserve - Automatic time tracker for Mac

sources.entry: Qbserve - Automatic time tracking with projects, timesheets, and productivity insights.

summary.name: Qbserve
summary.one_liner: Qbserve is an automatic time tracker for Mac that logs app, document, and website activity to produce productivity reports, project timesheets, and invoices.
use_cases: tracking billable hours for freelance projects
auditing daily app and website usage
generating client invoices from recorded time
exporting time data to JSON or CSV
summary.what_it_does: Qbserve runs on macOS and automatically records time spent in apps, documents, window titles, and websites, with productivity ratings for over 8,100 sites, apps and games. Users create rules that assign tracked time to projects when a document path or browser address contains a chosen string, such as a project name. Timesheets show an activity summary, timeline and notes for each hour, and undetected time can be assigned at the end of the day. Invoice items are generated from recorded time and can be customized, with invoices available in 18 languages. Data can be exported to JSON and CSV, optionally on a schedule.
notable: Project rules match document paths and browser addresses to bill time automatically
All tracked data stored locally on the Mac and not sent anywhere, per the page
Productivity score shown in the menu bar with a color-changing icon
Invoice generation in 18 languages with JSON and CSV export
caveats: Mac-only; the page says it is built specifically for macOS
Site tracking in Firefox, Vivaldi, Opera and Yandex requires installing browser extensions; automatic detection covers Chrome and Safari
Some time, such as in sites or tools the rules cannot match, must be assigned manually in timesheets
